links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT 3.5 vs 4.0 responses (word count, Flesch-Kincaid reading ease and grade level)
links.effect: Version 4.0 output was harder to read: more words, lower Flesch-Kincaid reading ease score, and higher Flesch-Kincaid grade level than 3.5. No numeric values given in the abstract.
links.quote: As for readability, there was a higher demand for readers to comprehend the output text in the 4.0 version (more counts of words; lower Flesch-Kincaid reading ease score; and higher Flesch-Kincaid grade level).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of ChatGPT (v3.5 vs 4.0) answering neurosurgical health management questions, evaluated by expert neurosurgeons for accuracy/consistency and readability formulas without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
